newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed after Wall St falters.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses mixed after Wall St falters.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Tuesday after Wall Street ended its record-breaking run and Europe's biggest phone company Deutsche Telekom lost ground following a storming global debut.
Germany's blue-chip DAX index gyrated around its opening levels as Germany's major telecommuncations operator joined the 30-share index the day after its debut with a weighting of 4.5 percent.
French shares recovered their losses by midday, but British shares swiftly erased opening gains.
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar slipped back from its overnight highs against the yen in choppy trade but was steady against the mark.
Bond markets saw German government bonds, or bunds, retain a firm bias in early trade, helping British government gilts to open 1/32 higher.

Worries about how long Wall Street's blistering rally can last continued to nag at European bourses after the Dow Industrials Average followed eight straight record closes on Monday with a one point decline.
In Germany, the stock market was dominated by Telekom. The DAX was up 10 points at one point but slipped into negative ground by mid-morning before recovering.

Telekom slipped below the 32.20 mark level it began trading at on Monday and by 1200 GMT was down 1.75 marks at 32.15. The shares earlier set bells ringing on the Tokyo stock market as Japanese investors and dealers rushed to trade the newly-listed share as they had in New York and Frankfurt.
In London, shares crept higher at the start of business but soon turned negative on concerns about Wall Street and caution ahead of next week's British budget.

"We've got the budget coming up on Tuesday. People are just sitting on their hands and when that happens the market tends to come off a bit," said one dealer. "And people are very distrusting of Wall Street."
The Dow was expected to open about 10 points lower, having soared by some 325 points, or about 5.4 percent, in the past two weeks.
"Without a lead from the U.S. this afternoon, we could end on either side of unchanged," said another dealer.
The utility sector stayed at the forefront after the Wall Street Journal said London Electricity may be the target of a 1.2 billion pound ($2 billion) offer from Entergy Corp of the United States.
French stocks were marginally higher by midday in a relatively calm market without much direction after spending most of the morning slightly down.
Eurotunnel was down 1.92 percent at 7.65 francs but off its lows after a fire in the Channel Tunnel between France and Britain forced the temporary closure of the rail link.

Euro Disney was off 1.31 percent at 11.30 francs after trading as low at 10.80 francs shortly after the open. The company reported a 77 percent rise in 1995-96 profits but the Paris theme park operator said it faced a tough year.
The dollar was steady against the mark after Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said the German central bank would welcome a more stable and stronger dollar.
Earlier reports quoting him as saying he saw no reason for the dollar to rise at the moment were a misunderstanding, he told reporters late on Monday.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.38 yen and 1.5037 marks, compared with 111.29 yen and 1.4996 marks in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 2.8 points at 3,959.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 0.88 of a point at 2,229.69.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 1.43 points at 2,765.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed easier at $378.30 against $379.10 on Monday afternoon and $379.70 in the morning. Silver was down two cents at $4.88.
